text.p: Here are highlights of stories in Romania's press on Friday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy:
Business:
ADEVARUL
- The leu sold at over 5,000 to the dollar at several retail currency shops on Thursday.
ROMANIA LIBERA
- Romania has never had a strategic programme for crediting and financing profitable companies, says Emil Cioflan, president of Renasterea Creditului Romanesc Credit Bank SA.
TINERETUL LIBER
- The national railway company SNCFR will sell 25,000 tonnes of scrap iron at an auction at the Bucharest commodities exchange on November 28.
ZIUA
- Romania will launch a 50,000 lei banknote on November 21.
LIBERTATEA
- Trading on the recently opened over-the-counter market has picked up this week.
CURIERUL NATIONAL

- Chase Manhattan Bank halted a $200 million credit to Romania's National Oil Company (CRP), recently suspended by a court order. The bank said the CRP should clarify the issue before getting the credit.
General:
ROMANIA LIBERA

- Soccer star Gica Hagi and another 23 Romanians playing at clubs abroad vote for Emil Constantinescu, the opposition Democratic Convention (CDR) candidate in Sunday's presidential run-offs with incumbent President Ion Iliescu.
- The newspaper publishes a full-page report on Romania's expenditure of millions of dollars in the United States allegedly to improve the country's image.
- The newspaper publishes a two-page report on Corneliu Coposu, leader of the opposition National Peasant Party (PNT-CD), who died a year ago.
ADEVARUL
- The ruling Party of Social Democracy is not reformist and three quarters of its members should be replaced by younger people, said former tennis star Ilie Nastase after he resigned from PDSR.
- Outgoing Foreign Minister Teodor Melescanu was elected a member of the UN commission for international law for a five-year term.
EVENIMENTUL ZILEI

- Two independent polling institutes will broadcast the results of their exit polls minutes after polling stations are closed in Sunday's run-off -- IRSOP on state television and IMAS on private PRO Tv.
- Outgoing Defence Minister Gheorghe Tinca will return to the foreign ministry. He was defeated in a bid to become senator on the PDSR list in the Transylvanian county of Cluj.
CRONICA ROMANA
- Of the 676 children sexually abused in Romania last year, 119 were 10 years old or younger.
LIBERTATEA
- Bucharest police chief said 2,000 police officers and 1,800 gendarmes will watch polling stations and party headquarters on Sunday.
- The Central Electoral Bureau said it would announce the official results from Sunday's presidential run-off by Wednesday, November 20.
- Bucharest has its first hostel for women attacked by their husbands.
DIMINEATA
- Outgoing Defence Minister Tinca said the army had done its duty and fulfilled the criteria for joining NATO.
CURIERUL NATIONAL
- The newspaper analyses the first face-to-face debate on state television between Iliescu and Constantinescu. ($=3,472 lei) -- Bucharest Newsroom 40-1 3120264
